6. The learned senior counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
7. He submits that the parties were in a consensual relationship and the applicant is eight years younger than the prosecutrix.

He submits that the relationship between the parties was not pretexted on any promise of marriage and the present FIR was lodged to wreak vengeance after the relationship between the parties turned sour.
He submits that there are no chats to this effect between the parties, but there are several videos and conversations where the prosecutrix threatened to falsely implicate the applicant.
8. He further submits that no tentative date or time of the alleged offences has been mentioned by the prosecutrix in her complaints.

He submits that although the CDR of the applicant shows that he was in Delhi from 27th- 31st May, 2023, however, he had never visited the apartment of the prosecutrix and the CDR also does not show that the applicant was present at or near the scene of the alleged offence either.
He submits that there is no proof of any intoxicating material ever being given to the prosecutrix.
He further submits that no particulars as to when the abortion was actually done is given either.

18. In the present case, while the applicant has admitted to the relationship between the parties, it is argued that he never made any promise to marry the prosecutrix.
It is pertinent to note that as per prosecution, the parties were known to each other since October, 2022.
As alleged in the FIR, the first incident of rape took place in Delhi.
The incident is alleged to have taken place in May, 2023.
However, in her deposition, the victim alleged that the applicant had forcefully established sexual relations with her in February, 2023 in Mumbai.

19 . It is also pointed out that the complainant has registered a similar case against a common acquaintance of the parties where she alleged that the accused therein had expressed his intention to This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/07/2025 at 22:09:02 marry her and established sexual relations with her on that pretext in July, 2022.
She further alleged that the said accused had not returned the money that she had lent to him and he had clicked her intimate photographs without her consent.

Another FIR has been registered at the instance of the prosecutrix against the applicant in Mumbai on similar allegations as well, where she has narrated certain incidents that took place between her and the applicant in Mumbai.

20. It is pertinent to note that apart from the ground of double jeopardy, while granting bail to the applicant in the FIR lodged in Mumbai, the learned Sessions Court in Mumbai observed that the allegations are in relation to incidents which precede the registration of FIR in Delhi.

It was also observed that perusal of that FIR suggested that the relationship between the parties was prima facie consensual in nature and the prosecutrix had continued to establish sexual relations with the applicant even after he allegedly shared her intimate photos.
The learned Sessions Court has also taken note of the case lodged by the prosecutrix against the mutual acquaintance of the parties on similar allegations as well.
21. Prima facie, at this stage, the aforesaid aspects cast a doubt on the veracity of the case of the prosecution.

22. It is also relevant to note that the FIR ultimately came to be registered at the end of January,
2024, which suggests that the parties were in a relationship for more than seven months at least.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Pramod Suryabhan Pawar v. The State of Maharashtra & Anr. : (2019) 9 SCC 608, has summarised the legal position when a woman complains of sexual intercourse on a false promise of marriage.

To summarise the legal position that emerges from the above cases, the "consent" of a woman with respect to Section 375 must involve an active and reasoned deliberation towards the proposed act.
To establish whether the "consent" was vitiated by a "misconception of fact" arising out of a promise to marry, two propositions must be established.
The promise of marriage must have been a false promise, given in bad faith and with no intention of being adhered to at the time it was given.

The false promise itself must be of immediate relevance, or bear a direct nexus to the woman's decision to engage in the sexual act."
23.
It is to be seen whether the person who has made the promise to marry was dishonest from the beginning and had no intention of upholding his word even at the time of making such a promise.
Mere breach of a promise to marry at a belated stage after significant time has elapsed cannot be termed as a false promise.
If the promise to marry was ever given by the applicant, or if the same was given in bad faith to induce the consent of the prosecutrix, cannot be established at this stage,
and the same would be a matter of trial, however, in the facts of the present case, the benefit of the inconsistencies has to go to the applicant.
24. The applicant was arrested on 17.07.2024 and he is in custody since then.
The investigation is complete and the matter is at the stage of examination of prosecution witnesses.
The examination of the prosecutrix has been substantially completed and only her testimony in relation to the FSL result remains to be conducted.
The matter has already been adjourned once at the request of State for conclusion of the examination of the prosecutrix.
It is unclear as to why the examination of the prosecutrix has been kept pending awaiting the FSL results.
Despite request of this Court, the examination of the prosecutrix is not yet concluded and this Court does not consider it apposite to keep the matter pending any longer.

The object is neither punitive nor preventive and the deprivation of liberty has been considered as a punishment.
26. It is pointed out that the applicant was declared as a proclaimed offender and there is threat that he may attempt to evade trial if he is granted bail.
It is pertinent to note that after his arrest, the applicant was granted interim bail and he did not misuse the liberty.
27. It is also argued that the victim is receiving threats.

It is relevant to note that the learned Trial Court has already taken note of the said aspect and noted the submission of the Investigating Officer that necessary protection will be provided to the victim if required after assessment of security.

Moreover, the said threats have not been directly linked to the applicant and bail ought not to be Abhishek Sharma vs State Of Delhi & Anr on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58268882/

29. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the applicant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond for a sum of 20,000/- with two sureties of the like amount, subject to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court, on the following conditions:
a.

The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case or tamper with the evidence of the case, in any manner whatsoever;
b.
The applicant shall under no circumstance leave the
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/07/2025 at 22:09:02 boundaries of the country without permission of the learned Trial Court;
c. The applicant shall appear before the learned Trial Court as and when directed;
d. The applicant shall provide the address where he would be residing after his release and shall not change the address without informing the concerned IO/ SHO;
e. The applicant shall, upon his release, give his mobile number to the concerned IO/SHO and shall keep his mobile phones switched on at all times.
30. In the event of there being any FIR/ DD entry/ complaint lodged against the applicant, it would be open to the State to seek redressal by filing an application seeking cancellation of bail.

31. It is clarified that any observations made in the present order are for the purpose of deciding the present bail application and should not influence the outcome of the trial and also not be taken as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case.
32. The bail application is allowed in the aforementioned terms.
